sentences.text: I spent the morning siphoning debris from between the spiderwood branches so nothing would cloud the final photographs. The turret ring, wedged solid with compacted chalk, refused the crane's first pull. After the awards, competitors swapped trimming techniques over cold noodles, sketching hardscape ideas on the backs of their scoring sheets. Careful stratigraphy matters more than speed here — the burn layer above the hull dates the engagement. Newcomers learn the hard way that a focal point placed dead center costs points on every judge's sheet. Honestly, I expected bones; instead we lifted a periscope housing, intact, glass and all. The judges docked her two points because the hairgrass carpet had lifted near the front glass overnight. Under the sponson lay forty-three cartridge cases, each one bagged, labeled, and logged before dark. By noon the convention hall smelled of wet soil and glue, and every competitor was pretending not to study the neighboring entries. Before the hull travels anywhere, the museum's registrar wants a complete condition report on file. Photography day means blackout curtains, a rented strobe, and forty minutes of coaxing the rummynose tetras into the golden-ratio zone. A curator photographed each road wheel in situ, numbering them against the site grid. Nobody expected the ninety-centimeter iwagumi to beat last year's champion, yet there it sat, first-place ribbon taped to its cabinet. Deeper down the soil turns anaerobic and blue-grey, which is why any steel survived at all. We hauled buckets down the loading dock at dawn, praying the amano shrimp had survived the drive from Portland. Fragments of a crewman's map case emerged from the silt beside the driver's position. "Your negative space carries the whole composition," the Belgian judge told him, tapping the empty sand foreground. Corrosion had welded the hatch shut, so the team documented the interior with a borescope. His bucephalandra had melted two weeks before judging; he entered anyway. Soil samples from stratum IV still smell faintly of diesel, eighty years on. What is the meaning of the word tank?
